overview: This enum chooses which full-face animation a character plays during battle and cutscenes.

None.simple: The character keeps its current facial animation.
None.technical: SetFacial clears bDefaultFacial and returns before choosing an animation. FGameDataTableRow_Attack defaults CharacterFacial to None.

Default.simple: The character returns to its normal face and can blink.
Default.technical: SetFacial sets bDefaultFacial true and plays Facial_Default. The blink driver reads bDefaultFacial along with the owner facial-blink setting. Battle states, blow actions, and guard breaks call this value to restore the normal face.

Damage.simple: The character makes a pain face when hit.
Damage.technical: SetFacial maps this value to GAnimName_Facial_Damage and plays Facial_Damage. GameCharacterAction_Damage passes it to SetFacial on the damage action.

Pinch.simple: The character makes a strained or clenched face.
Pinch.technical: SetFacial maps this value to GAnimName_Facial_Pinch and plays Facial_Pinch.

Surprised.simple: The character makes a surprised face.
Surprised.technical: SetFacial maps this value to GAnimName_Facial_Surprised and plays Facial_Surprised.

Dead.simple: The character makes a defeated face.
Dead.technical: SetFacial maps this value to GAnimName_Facial_Dead and plays Facial_Dead. Blow actions pass it to SetFacial when a character is defeated.

Attack_01.simple: The character makes an attack face.
Attack_01.technical: SetFacial maps this value to GAnimName_Facial_Attack_01 and plays Facial_Attack_01. StartAttack passes AttackRow->CharacterFacial directly to SetFacial, and the exported Attack rows use this value.

Invalid.simple: The character clears the current full-face animation.
Invalid.technical: SetFacial clears bDefaultFacial, then stops the FacialGroup montages with a zero blend time. Animation notify objects default to Invalid, and converter cleanup passes Invalid to clear the facial state.

notes: SetFacial does nothing unless bFacialAvailable is true.
SetFacial writes bDefaultFacial before handling None and Invalid. Only Default leaves that flag true, and the blink driver reads it to decide whether blinking is allowed.
The sequencer facial module validates the integer with StaticEnum before converting it to EGameCharacterFacial. Converter cleanup calls SetFacial with Invalid directly.
These values select full-face assets and are separate from EGameCharacterFacialPartsMouth and the other facial-part enums.
